label: Le Petit Trianon playhouse
more: A split-log playhouse with kitchen, scullery and sitting room, built near the house. Historic England says it was for the Earl's children, who were grown by 1856, so grandchildren would fit better; no source settles it. The name echoes Marie Antoinette's Petit Trianon at Versailles.

label: French Parterre restored to the Earl's design
more: After a full excavation found the original beds and gravel, English Heritage restored the parterre to Earl de Grey's 1830s design. It had been simplified in the early 1900s to make it easier to maintain.

label: Restoration of the parterre's Cheere statues begins
more: Conservators steamed off peeling paint from Venus and Adonis and Aeneas and Anchises, each over 3 metres tall, and repainted them to look like marble. It was the first phase of a wider statue project.
